q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b.name AS beer, MIN(s.price) AS price, sb.name AS bar FROM beer AS b LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.beer LEFT JOIN bar AS sb ON s.bar = sb.name AND s.price = (SELECT MIN(s2.price) FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.beer = b.name) OR (s.price IS NULL AND sb.name IS NULL) GROUP BY b.name, sb.name, s.price ORDER BY b.name, s.price

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT b.name AS beer, MIN(s.price) AS price, sb.name AS bar FROM beer AS b LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.beer LEFT JOIN bar AS sb ON s.bar = sb.name AND s.price = (SELECT MIN(s2.price) FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.beer = b.name) OR (s.price IS NULL AND sb.name IS NULL) GROUP BY b.name, sb.name, s.price ORDER BY b.name, s.price
counterexample: INSERT INTO beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('BeerA', 'BrewerX'); INSERT INTO bar (name, address) VALUES ('Bar1', 'Address1'), ('Bar2', 'Address2'); INSERT INTO serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('Bar1', 'BeerA', 10.00), ('Bar2', 'BeerA', 10.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they join the 'serves' table in different ways, which affects the results, especially when there are multiple bars serving the same beer at the same price.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when there are multiple bars serving the same beer at the same price. In this case, Q1 will return all such bars, while Q2 will only return one of them due to the GROUP BY clause.
